<!-- docs-drift-check -->
### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **2** package(s): `@objectstack/lint`, `@objectstack/spec`, touching **7** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **3** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/spec/authorable-surface/security.json`, `packages/spec/liveness/permission.json`, `packages/spec/liveness/state-counts/permission.md`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**3** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/data-modeling/fields.mdx`  _(via rollupSourceUnreadableReason (literal, a string literal in FieldPermissionSchema))_
- `content/docs/deployment/validating-metadata.mdx`  _(via rollupSourceUnreadableReason (literal, a string literal in FieldPermissionSchema))_
- `content/docs/protocol/objectql/security.mdx`  _(via FieldPermissionSchema (symbol, a top-level const), rollupSourceUnreadableReason (literal, a string literal in FieldPermissionSchema))_

⛔ **1** release-owned page(s) also name something this change touched. These are **read-only**:

- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-0.mdx`  _(via FieldPermissionSchema (symbol, a top-level const))_

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **3** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/spec/authorable-surface/security.json`, `packages/spec/liveness/permission.json`, `packages/spec/liveness/state-counts/permission.md`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **1** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **247** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **182** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **182**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **123** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **173** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json c12fe6649ffeb8a83dae916e8c420fa68c88a2cc` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `d4146b7007524673a7ac7e6784755d05954d9528` — the merge of head `b61b6d75111e8747f7fcfec1abfb3703cf1a535d` into base `c12fe6649ffeb8a83dae916e8c420fa68c88a2cc`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin d4146b7007524673a7ac7e6784755d05954d9528 && git checkout d4146b7007524673a7ac7e6784755d05954d9528
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin c12fe6649ffeb8a83dae916e8c420fa68c88a2cc b61b6d75111e8747f7fcfec1abfb3703cf1a535d && git checkout -B drift-repro c12fe6649ffeb8a83dae916e8c420fa68c88a2cc && git merge --no-ff b61b6d75111e8747f7fcfec1abfb3703cf1a535d

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json c12fe6649ffeb8a83dae916e8c420fa68c88a2cc
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs c12fe6649ffeb8a83dae916e8c420fa68c88a2cc` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `7a8180f2f6ca2fe580d1bc7559828d0012f022f5`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/security/permission.zod.ts + packages/lint/src/validate-rollup-source-visibility.ts, packages/lint/src/rule-explanations.ts, packages/spec/liveness/permission.json

How this head was read: the net diff of `6b6146d0c4dfa00c67e63b635f2adada3b52cad2` against its merge-base with `main` from git objects (13 files), plus the one file the head commit `7a8180f2` adds on top of it, `content/docs/protocol/objectql/security.mdx` (+4/-1), read from the PR's file list because that commit is not in the local object store. The PR file list at this head (14 files, +330/-13) differs from the 13-file diff by that one prose file only; the hunks of the other 13 files in the PR file list match the local diff. Card #34664 body and all five comments, the PR body, and the check-runs on this head were read. Nothing was built or run.

Security-touching: yes (the field-level permission surface of a permission set).

### ① Derived judgments

- Accept-set of `FieldPermissionSchema`: widened by one optional string key, `rollupSourceUnreadableReason`. Right. The shipped name and placement match the seat's name ruling 6943835606 on the card exactly (the key, on the set's `fields` entry, value a reason string, no separate type).
- New refusals, both confined to inputs that carry the new key, so nothing that parsed on `main` is refused. Right.
  - Blank reason: `z.string().refine(NON_BLANK_STRING, ...)` on the key itself, path `rollupSourceUnreadableReason`, message `FIELD_PERMISSION_ROLLUP_REASON_BLANK`. `NON_BLANK_STRING` is the shared self-declaring predicate, so the published JSON Schema carries the non-blank pattern.
  - Reason beside `readable: false`: a second object-level `.refine`, path `['rollupSourceUnreadableReason']`, message `FIELD_PERMISSION_ROLLUP_REASON_ON_HIDDEN`. It runs on the defaulted value, so an absent `readable` (default `true`) is accepted and only a literal `false` is refused, which is the ruling's "readable that is not true". The object-level refine is a dropped refinement in the JSON Schema; `dropped-refinements.baseline.json` already declares the root site of `security/FieldPermission` (for the `when` rule) and a second refine at the same site adds no row; the key's `describe` states the rule in prose, as the `when` rule does.
- Both refusals are real pins in `permission.test.ts`: three blank spellings with the message asserted, a non-string, and the `readable: false` case asserted by issue path and message; the accept case, the no-materialisation case and the `PermissionSetSchema.fields` case are pinned too.
- Where the refusal applies: every parse of `FieldPermissionSchema`, which is `PermissionSetSchema.fields` and `GetObjectPermissionsResponseSchema.fieldPermissions`. On the permission set that is right. On the response it is inert: read in the live tree, no server code implements `getObjectPermissions` (the protocol method is optional and only the client re-exports the type), and both field merges (`PermissionEvaluator.getFieldPermissions`, `buildEffectiveFieldPermissions`) build fresh `{ readable, editable }` entries from votes and never copy an authored entry, so the reason does not reach `/auth/me/permissions` or any per-object field projection. The jsdoc sentence "the server never sends it on the permission responses that reuse this shape" holds. No disclosure of author notes through the runtime responses; the reason is visible only where the permission set's own metadata is, like its description. The reuse is not a reason to move the key: the published response reference now lists the key, with a description that says the runtime does not read it. Accepted as the ruling decided.
- Lint public surface: `security-rollup-source-unreadable` can now be emitted at `info` (same rule id, path extended to the key, message suffixed with the quoted reason, a different hint). Right, and stated in the rule's docblock table. The one consumer that filters by id without severity, `packages/qa/scenarios/src/runner/orchestrate.ts#rollupSourceCharges`, was read: its message patterns are anchored at the start and unanchored at the end, so the suffixed message still reads and a reason cannot spoof a clause; an acknowledged pair is still charged, which is the right posture for the eval.
- Generated and ledger surfaces: `authorable-surface/security.json` gains exactly `security/FieldPermission:rollupSourceUnreadableReason` in sorted position; `liveness/state-counts/permission.md` moves 40 to 41 live and 44 to 45 classified, consistent with one new live row. Right.
- Liveness (ADR-0049): the row names `validate-rollup-source-visibility.ts#acknowledgedReason` as the reader, which is true in the tree, says the runtime reads no part of the key, which the merge code confirms, and cites the dashboard `widgets.suppressWarnings` precedent for a live authoring-only consumer, which exists in `liveness/dashboard.json`. The `Spec property liveness` check concluded success on this head.

### ② Semver level

Clause-②: yes (widening) — one new optional authorable key; `Metadata-protocol: added`. The line is on the PR body and in the changeset, and both agree with the diff.

The changeset declares `@objectstack/spec` minor and `@objectstack/lint` minor. Those are the only two published packages the diff touches (the rest is `content/docs` prose and spec ledgers inside the spec package); both sit in the fixed version group. Minor is the right level for an additive key and an additive lint behaviour. `Check Changeset` concluded success on this head (both runs).

### ③ Boundary flags

- Dev `open_questions`: one entry, "Contract review owed at head 6b6146d0". Answered by this record, on the head the PR moved to; the only change since is the one prose file named above.
- Dev `security_findings`: none. Dev `deviations`: none.
- Dev `out_of_scope_findings`: the skill line and eval go to #34742. Judged: `skills/objectstack-data/rules/relationships.md` teaches "Never finish with `security-rollup-source-unreadable` standing" with two remedies (grant the child read, or mask the summary). After this PR that text is incomplete, not wrong: both remedies still work, the metadata it produces still parses, and the scenario runner still charges an acknowledged pair, so the stricter teaching stays consistent with its own eval. No published skill teaches something this PR makes false. The deferral holds; #34742 should decide whether the skill names the acknowledgement at all, given the eval charges it.
- PR-body acceptance note "a stale acknowledgement is not reported": see N3.
- SQL push-down: not applicable. The diff adds no data access, no id materialisation and no join; the rule reads authored metadata in memory.
- Check-runs on this head. Concluded success: Governed Surface Queue Guard, Spec property liveness, Check Changeset, Check PR Size, Check Documentation Links, Flag docs affected by code changes, PR-body guards (the rerun; the first run was cancelled and superseded), Lint · PM dispatch-gates, Lint · scoped · tooling self-tests, Dogfood Regression Gate, Plan Test Core shards, Plan Test UI shards, filter, Auto Label. Skipped by design: the opt-in and schedule jobs. PENDING when this record was written, and therefore not verdicts: Type Check · workspace, Type Check · source gates, Type Check · consumer gates, Type Check · debt ledger, Lint · ESLint, Lint · repo and tooling gates, Lint · docs and code guards, Lint · CI, release and engine gates, Lint · scoped · query-options erasure, Lint · scoped · slot lookup and corpus, Build Core, Build Docs, Build UI Deps, Live E2E UI, Test Core 1/8 to 8/8. No check had concluded failure. The generated-artefact, typecheck and test families are among the pending ones; the seat reads their conclusions before adopting this record.

### ④ Design judgment

`packages/spec/src/security/permission.zod.ts` against ruling 6943835606 and its first consumer (the lint rule):

- The key, its two refusals, their placement, paths and messages implement the ruling as written, and the first consumer reads exactly the shape the schema accepts (`acknowledgedReason` reads the set's own entry for the column and requires a non-blank string; a parsed set and a raw set answer the same, pinned).

S1 (should-fix) — the published text says the acknowledgement "changes nothing at runtime: the column is read under the parent field's own field-level security either way", and the jsdoc says "the field merge, the read mask ... are unchanged". That is true of the key and false of the act the key requires. The key can only be written on a `fields` entry, and an entry is a declaring vote: in the field merge only sets that declare an entry vote, most permissive wins, and a parsed entry defaults `readable: true` (`fieldPermissionVote`, `getFieldPermissions`, `buildEffectiveFieldPermissions`, read in the live tree; the rule's own hint says "to keep it for some holders, declare readable: true in the sets they hold"). So a set that had NO entry for the summary column and gains one only to carry the reason now votes `readable: true`, and for every user who also holds a set that masks that column with `readable: false` the mask stops binding. In the card's own scenario the sets are service, marketing and the default set; an entry on a set every user holds defeats every other set's mask of that total. The behaviour is the documented merge and may well be what the author means, but the describe, the jsdoc, `rule-explanations.ts`, `fields.mdx` and the new `security.mdx` note all tell the author the edit is runtime-neutral, on a security surface, at the moment they are adding a read vote. Fix: one sentence in the key's `describe` and jsdoc (then regenerated references), repeated in the rule explanation and `fields.mdx`: the entry that carries the reason is an ordinary declaring entry and votes `readable: true` in the field merge, so on a set that had no entry for the column it restores the column for holders whose other sets mask it. No behaviour change is asked for.

S2 (should-fix) — the new cross-key refusal has a second authoring door that this PR leaves able to produce the refused shape. Read, not reviewed: `ui/packages/app-shell/src/views/metadata-admin/PermissionMatrixEditor.tsx#updateFieldPerm` starts from the stored entry as is (`fieldRuleSeed` returns the entry), spreads it, and on Read off deletes `when` only, with the comment that the spec refuses `when` beside `readable: false` so the matrix "never authors that shape". With an entry that carries `rollupSourceUnreadableReason`, Read off now yields `readable: false` beside the reason, which this schema refuses; the matrix has no control that shows or clears the key, so an admin taking the very remedy the acknowledged finding's hint names (stop the set reading the column) meets a refused save with no in-editor way out. The failure is closed (nothing is widened or lost). Separately `permission-slice.ts#withFieldBits` (the bulk shortcuts) rebuilds the entry keeping `when` and silently drops the reason; that direction is safe (the warning returns) but it is an unannounced loss of authored text. That the save door parses with the spec is taken from the editor's own `when` comment, not traced further. Fix: mirror the `when` cascade for the new key in the matrix (Read off clears it; the bulk shortcut either carries or deliberately drops it, said in the comment), in this PR or on a follow-up card the seat files and names here; either disposal closes S2.

`packages/lint/src/validate-rollup-source-visibility.ts` against the contract, sentence by sentence:

- "that one finding, this set and this column": holds. The reason is read from `set.fields[column]` of the set being judged, with `column` the parent object and summary field name; nothing is read object-wide, set-wide or from a co-held set. All three arms of the rule (child object, aggregated field, filter field) go through the same closure, and each set and column yields at most one finding.
- "every other finding unchanged": holds. The unacknowledged branch is byte-identical to `main` (severity, path, message, hint); the row-scoped finding does not go through the closure.
- "quotes the reason": the trimmed reason is appended in double quotes after the full original message, so the pair and the cause stay readable. It is plain text into the finding message; no markup or shell sink was found on the path read.
- A raw blank reason acknowledges nothing; a raw `readable: false` entry never reaches the closure because the set is first judged not to read the column. Both agree with the schema's refusals.
- The new test pins the downgrade (severity, quoted reason, path), and the non-downgrade of the neighbours: another column of the same set, another set on the same column, and the row-scoped note; the control without the key is pinned in the same file.

`packages/lint/src/rule-explanations.ts`: the new paragraph agrees with the behaviour (one set, one column, note quoting the reason, neighbours and the row-scope note as before, the two refusals). It carries the S1 sentence.

`packages/spec/liveness/permission.json`: agrees with the tree, as judged under ①.

Prose read for agreement with the schema only: `content/docs/data-modeling/fields.mdx`, `content/docs/deployment/validating-metadata.mdx`, `content/docs/protocol/objectql/security.mdx` (the file the head commit adds), and the two generated reference pages. All agree with the schema and the rule, apart from the S1 sentence and N2. The `security.mdx` link target `fields#calculation-types` exists (heading "Calculation Types"), and the link check concluded success.

Nits (no effect on correctness or the contract):

- N1 — `FIELD_PERMISSION_ROLLUP_REASON_ON_HIDDEN` says the entry "hides the column and there is no read to acknowledge". For a set that holds Modify All on the parent, `readable: false` is inert and the set still reads the column; the refusal is still right (the fix it names, `readable: true`, is correct) but the stated cause is not true in that corner.
- N2 — `security.mdx` comments the key as "on a summary column only". The schema accepts it on any entry; "meaningful only on a summary column" is what is true.
- N3 — a reason on an entry that raises no finding today (a non-summary column, or a set that can currently read the child) is silent, as the PR body says. It also pre-acknowledges: if the child read is later removed, the finding first appears already at `info`. The seat chose not to report stale acknowledgements in this PR; a follow-up card is the right home.
- N4 — the new lint suite acknowledges only the child-object arm. The aggregated-field and filter-field arms share the closure, so they are covered by construction, not by a pin.
- N5 — the reason is interpolated between double quotes without escaping, so a reason containing a double quote or a line break renders raw in the message. Cosmetic.

S1 and S2 are open on this head. Neither changes a parse result or the rule's judgment, so the verdict is PASS on the contract as ruled; each fix that moves a file in Scope owes a delta review on the new head.

Implemented-by: `claude/project-thread-wq8blv`
Reviewed-by: `session_01ADHkmP44onN8RMzsPMqjRq`

**VERDICT: PASS**
